coarse_skill_concept: Debug C/C++ defects that are invisible at the language surface, including memory corruption that manifests only in release builds and template instantiation failures under older C++ standards.

task_judgments.reason: Directly requires debugging a release-mode crash by reproducing it, analyzing coredumps, and tracing through libstdc++ static-cleanup internals to find optimizer-exposed undefined behavior.
Requires statically identifying which post-C++11 features are used and rewriting with recursive template metaprogramming — no runtime debugging, coredump analysis, or UB tracing involved.

final_groups.skill_concept: Diagnose and fix C++ crashes that appear only in release builds by reproducing the crash, reading coredumps/backtraces, tracing optimizer-exposed undefined behavior through standard-library internals (e.g., allocator or locale static-cleanup paths), and correcting the underlying UB.
final_groups.reasoning: The task is purely a runtime debugging exercise: reproduce the release-only crash, extract a backtrace, locate the UB in the custom heap or libstdc++ destructor chain, and patch it — all steps that form a coherent runtime-debugging procedure.

final_groups.skill_concept: Port a modern C++ template to C++11 by identifying unavailable language features (fold expressions, if constexpr, C++14/17 standard-library additions) and replacing them with equivalent C++11 recursive template specialization or trait-based metaprogramming.
final_groups.reasoning: The task requires a static code-adaptation procedure: read the header, identify the post-C++11 construct, and rewrite it using C++11-legal recursive template structs — no runtime analysis or UB diagnosis is involved.
